text:
Ashwin: heads-up: alert 'otel-span-loss' just fired across ap-northeast and eu-west clusters. grafana shows a sudden spike in otel_exporter_dropped_spans_total and end-to-end trace durations jump. GPU pools around 10.2.1.* are seeing high queueing at the otlp-gateway.

Maria: seeing the same. Prom query: `sum(rate(otel_exporter_dropped_spans_total[1m])) by (cluster)` -> ap-northeast ~120/s. dashboard fleet/traces-overview shows gateway batch queue length steady at ~800 for ~30s.

Ben: quick log tail from otlp-gateway: ```2026-03-18T12:34:10Z WARN exporter/backpressure: buffer_full, dropping spans; dropped=83 gateway_queue_len=812 batch_max=1024``` Also a bunch of 429s from the collector to clickhouse-backend.

Jana: could be downstream backpressure + GPU pod saturation. Autoscaler didn't spin up new gpu-nodes because node-provisioner blocked on ephemeral IP exhaustion in ap-northeast. I'm looking into IP pool exhaustion ticket.

Liam: interestingly, traceparent headers are intact at ingress, but our gateway is applying TTL per-span and discarding after 8s of queuing: `span_ttl_seconds=8` — that was lowered in the last tuning patch to improve memory footprint. Maybe too aggressive under burst.

Ashwin: proposal: 1) temporarily raise span_ttl_seconds to 20 in otlp-gateway config; 2) enable backpressure shed policy to prefer low-sampling A-tier requests instead of bulk dropping; 3) reduce collector batch_max to 512 to lower latency. Anyone object?

Maria: +1 for ttl bump. But we should be careful with cost — holding spans longer increases egress/storage during burst. Maybe apply per-namespace TTL: non-prod = 8s, prod = 20s.

Ben: config patch I'm going to test on canary: 
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 5s
    send_batch_size: 512
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    max_concurrent_requests: 32
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```
I'll push to canary namespace and watch `sum(rate(otel_exporter_dropped_spans_total[1m]))` and `gateway_queue_len`.

Jana: also, can we enable tail-sampling by route? For heavy GPU inference paths we keep 100% sampling for error events only, otherwise 10%. That should reduce burst volume while preserving quality.

Liam: FYI, autoscaler PR #4226 is blocked on ipam fix. If we don't free IPs soon, autoscaler won't provision extra GPU nodes and we'll keep hitting backend throttles. I'll ping infra on the IPAM thread.

infra-bot: deploy-canary:collector-config-18876 applied to cluster ap-northeast-canary by Ben at 1887654355.

Ashwin: thanks. After canary run (5m), if no regressions i'll roll the ttl change to prod and flip tail-sampling rules. Also opening a follow-up to evaluate alert thresholds — current otel-span-loss alert fires on any >5/min which is noisy for transient autoscaler races. Suggest `sum(rate(otel_exporter_dropped_spans_total[5m])) > 50` aggregated by region.

Maria: noted — I'll update the alert runbook with the new query and include steps: check IPAM, check gateway queue, check collector backpressure metrics, and roll back TTL change.

Ben: canary metrics look promising so far: dropped_spans down to ~10/s, queue_len stable ~200. Will promote in 2m if stays green.

Jana: postmortem action items: 1) increase default span_ttl_seconds in Gateway chart; 2) per-route tail-sampling policy for GPU inference; 3) IPAM capacity alert; 4) evaluate collector batching defaults to reduce 429s.

Liam: adding a Grafana panel for `otel_exporter_dropped_spans_total` annotated with `node_autoscaler_events` and `ipam_exhaustion` events, should help correlate faster.

Ashwin: perfect. If Ben promotes, I'll monitor SLO page and mute the noisy alert for 10m during roll. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: alert mute applied (otel-span-loss) for 10m by Ashwin at 1887654388.

Ben: promo done at 1887654389 — prod roll started. Watching now.

Maria: seeing stabilizing traces. Keep an eye for cost spike. We'll follow up with cost/quality tradeoff analysis tomorrow.

Ashwin: thanks team, will close thread after 24h observation. If anything else pops up, call it out here. :rocket:
